subject: MAP Review: Queueing, Batching & Caching Assumptions for Cost Model
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Anthony Bueno <anthony.bueno@helixmed.com>, HelixMed Procurement <procurement@helixmed.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: MAP Draft: queueing/batching/caching assumptions — please review

Anthony / team,

Thanks for yesterday's call — attached is a clean MAP draft (HLX-MAP_v0.3.xlsx) and the token-level model (helix-token-econ-model.csv) that underpins the pricing section. I highlighted the explicit assumptions around request size distribution, batching, and caching on the "Cost" tab so we can align before procurement reviews. Quick summary of the assumptions we used: 

- Average request tokens (prompt + response): 420 tokens
- Expected production response length (95th percentile): 1,200 tokens
- Live batching: effective batch size 8 (conservative) — we used GPU microbatching 8–16 in the model
- Prefix / KV cache hit rate: 30% (first-pass conservative)
- Quantized model variant: int8 fallback with ~1.6x performance improvement vs fp16 in our test harness
- Pilot throughput target: 50 rps sustained with p90 latency < 400ms for short responses

Can you confirm the inputs above (particularly average token counts and acceptable latency SLOs) so we can lock the MAP milestones and target procurement date?

I've cc'd Rishi for commercial sign-off but will loop in Grace for a quick technical verification of the caching/batching numbers if you want deeper validation.

Attachments: HLX-MAP_v0.3.xlsx (Excel, 54 KB); helix-token-econ-model.csv (CSV, 12 KB)

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0148

From: Anthony Bueno <anthony.bueno@helixmed.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP Draft: queueing/batching/caching assumptions — please review

Karthik,

Thanks for the draft — the layout helps. A couple of clarifying questions from our ops and procurement teams before we push this into the MAP: 

1) Cache hit rate — you have 30% in the model. How sensitive is cost to that? Our workload has a lot of repeated forms but also many unique free-text notes. If hit rate is 15% vs 45% how does that change tokens/$ in your spreadsheet?

2) Batching assumptions — what are measurable prerequisites for hitting effective batch size 8 in production? For example, does that require a buffering window that would increase latency for interactive users?

3) For pilot pricing we need a clear breakout: tokens during pilot vs projected at scale; if caching improves over time we want to see a conservative and an optimistic scenario.

If helpful, please loop in your solutions engineer to validate the caching/batching behavior against the HelixMed usage patterns — we can share sample traces. Also cc'd procurement (procurement@helixmed.com) — target is to get the MAP agreed and PO issued by 10/01/2027.

—Anthony
Anthony Bueno
Head of Integrations | HelixMed
anthony.bueno@helixmed.com

Grace / Rishi,

Anthony raised three sticky items (cache sensitivity, batching prerequisites, pilot vs scale scenarios). Could you validate the model tabs in helix-token-econ-model.csv and recommend conservative/likely/optimistic values we should put into the MAP? Also want to call out any instrumentation we should add to the pilot to measure cache hit rate and effective batch size.

Notes: 
- Customer can share sample traces; sensitive data will be redacted.
- Procurement target: 2027-10-01 for PO.

Thanks — Karthik

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Anthony Bueno <anthony.bueno@helixmed.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: MAP Draft — technical validation and instrumentation suggestions

Karthik / Anthony,

Quick validation after reviewing the CSV and the sample traces Anthony offered (thanks): I recommend we update the MAP with the following conservative / baseline / optimistic set so procurement and ops have clear scenarios.

Conservative (MAP baseline):
- Avg tokens/request: 470 (higher due to verbose notes)
- Effective batch size: 6 (assume lower client concurrency during early pilot)
- KV/prefix cache hit: 25%
- Token cost sensitivity: at 25% cache vs 45% cache, per-token unit cost increases by ~27% in our model (line item: "net_token_units").

Baseline (recommended for MAP):
- Avg tokens/request: 420
- Effective batch size: 8
- KV/prefix cache hit: 35%
- Expect ~12–18% improvement in tokens/$ over conservative as caching matures to baseline.

Optimistic (scale ops):
- Avg tokens/request: 380 (prompt engineering + response truncation)
- Effective batch size: 12
- KV/prefix cache hit: 50%
- Combine with quantized model path yields ~1.9x cost improvement vs conservative table.

Instrumentation (pilot):
- Log per-request token counts and model variant used (fp16 vs quantized) — already supported via our token meter.
- Emit per-route "effective_batch_size" metric and GPU microbatch occupancy (helps validate 8->12 trend).
- Add a lightweight cache diagnostics endpoint returning hit/miss counters per prefix key class every 1h.
- Tag pilot requests with "pilot:true" for sampling and isolating telemetry.

I'll attach a short note (response-security-q.pdf) with the telemetry fields and RBAC considerations for HelixMed's infra team — nothing sensitive, just field names. If HelixMed wants, we can run a 48–72 hour controlled pilot to measure actual batch occupancy and cache hit growth; the MAP can include a gated milestone that moves from "baseline" to "optimistic" pricing after successful instrumentation and 7-day stability window.

Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Anthony Bueno <anthony.bueno@helixmed.com>, HelixMed Procurement <procurement@helixmed.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: MAP update & next steps — proposed pilot gating and target PO date

Anthony / procurement team,

Thanks — based on Grace's validation we've updated the MAP and attached a redline (HLX-MAP_v0.3.xlsx) with the conservative/baseline/optimistic scenarios surfaced on the Cost tab. Key changes (short):

- MAP baseline updated to: avg 420 tokens, effective batch size = 8, cache hit = 35%
- Pilot instrumentation tasks added as MAP milestones (emit batch occupancy, token meter tags, cache hit counters) — see milestone 2.2
- Pricing: pilot runs under conservative prices; upon successful 7-day stability gate showing batch occupancy >= 8 and cache hit >= 30% we move to baseline pricing in the MAP pricing sheet.
- Proposed procurement / PO window: target issuance by 2027-10-01 per your ask. If we can sign the MAP this week we'll schedule the pilot for the week of 2027-10-10.

Next steps for HelixMed: 
1) Confirm procurement target date (10/01) and PO approver.
2) Share sanitized traces for a 48h pre-pilot validation (Grace will validate and return instrumentation plan).
3) Confirm stakeholder for pilot gating (ops owner + procurement rep).

DocuSign/PO link will be added to the MAP once procurement confirms. Let me know if you'd like a short 30-minute call this week to walk through the instrumentation checklist.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
